    Erisian Empire

    Emperor Hermes Kennensbach¶

    The current Emperor, Hermes Kennensbach, is widely regarded as intelligent and capable. He has:

    • Won several battles personally, establishing himself as a competent military leader.
    • Demonstrated strong economic sense — cutting taxes, reforming trade policies.
    • Attempted to centralize the Empire somewhat, pushing back against the centrifugal forces of countism.

    Despite his competence, he is failing. The Empire cracks regardless of his efforts — as if the entire machine were running without oil, doomed to break no matter how skillfully it is maintained. Financial collapse looms. Institutional decay accelerates. His centralization efforts stall.

    Character: - Not evil. Good-willed and genuinely wants to stabilize the Empire. - The Shadows attempted to co-opt him — it never worked. He does not know about the Shadows, but he is deeply suspicious of the Erisian Church. He has smelled that something is not right there. He has never said so publicly. - Irascible and very serious — not a warm man, but a fair one. - Willing to help take down the Church if provided with the truth about everything. - Has a wife, four daughters, and five sons. Maintains multiple affairs. - Getting old. His window for decisive action is closing.

    Church-State Relations¶

    The Erisian Empire is considered "the sword of the Erisian Church." The relationship is symbiotic:

    • The Church spends enormous amounts of money in the Empire and maintains extensive institutions within its borders — cathedrals, monasteries, schools, courts.
    • The Empire provides military force, political legitimacy, and the physical enforcement of Church doctrine.
    • In theory, the Church and Empire are partners. In practice, the tension between secular and religious authority is constant — and Hermes's private suspicions make it more complicated than anyone realizes.

    Species Relations¶

    Elves¶

    The Empire has a history of irrational, intense hatred toward Elves. They were heavily persecuted for centuries — the Great Elvish Persecution of 137 AGD was only the most organized expression of a deeper cultural hostility. Elves were hunted, expelled, or killed on sight in many imperial territories.

    Today, elves are legally permitted to live as citizens within the Empire. The laws have changed. But the culture has not. Elves are still seen with suspicion, treated with coldness, and viewed through narrowed eyes. They are tolerated, not welcomed.

    Outside the Empire, in other Erisdarian nations, elves face disdain as well — but the Empire's particular history makes its prejudice uniquely intense.

    Demons¶

    Demons are not seen with the same suspicion as elves. They trade within the Empire and travel freely. The stigma of the name "demon" persists — they are still taught as the antagonists in old histories and church texts — but centuries of exposure have worn down the fear. People tolerate demons, even if they do not embrace them. The old stories say demons are evil. The demon merchant buying grain at the market says otherwise. Most imperials have learned to live with the contradiction.

    Other Species¶

    Dwarves, Catmen, Beast Races, and other species are generally accepted. Dwarvstadt, a county within the Empire, is majority-dwarven and fully integrated into imperial governance.

    Subdivisions¶

    The Empire is divided into: - 3 Duchies: Kennberg, Prassen-Albridge, Mirenburg - 22 Counties (naming convention: -stadt) - 2 Free Cities: Kelensborgh, Tuvir - 1 Church State: Rroffran

    The Archduchy of the Kennberg serves as the imperial heartland and the Emperor's personal domain.

    Modern Challenges¶

    • Financial collapse — the Erilia currency faces severe strain as provinces operate with increasing autonomy.
    • Institutional decay — the crusades have died down; the Church can no longer enforce its will through pure military force.
    • Failing dogmas — laws like the polygamy ban are crumbling in peripheral territories.
    • Elvish resurgence — elven populations have stabilized; independent elvish states have re-entered the geopolitical arena.
    • The Emperor's age — Hermes Kennensbach will not rule forever, and the succession is uncertain.
